name: sensitivity conjecture
after: Before: the conjecture was attacked by combinatorial and Fourier-analytic means; the best known lower bound on the maximum degree of an induced subgraph on more than half the vertices of the n-cube was about (1/2 - o(1)) log n. After: one assigns a particular +/-1 signing to the edges of the n-cube, so that the signed adjacency matrix squares to n times the identity; its spectrum is therefore +/- sqrt(n), and Cauchy eigenvalue interlacing applied to any induced subgraph on more than half the vertices forces that subgraph to have maximum degree at least sqrt(n). The whole argument is a page.

name: finite field Kakeya
after: Before: bounds on the size of a Kakeya set in F_q^n were obtained by combinatorial incidence geometry and gave exponents strictly below n. After: one observes that a set too small to be a Kakeya set admits a nonzero polynomial of low degree vanishing on it; evaluating that polynomial along the lines in every direction and comparing leading terms forces a contradiction. The bound becomes essentially optimal and the proof is a few paragraphs.

name: cap set
after: Before: upper bounds for progression-free subsets of F_3^n came from Fourier analysis and density increment arguments, improving the trivial bound only by logarithmic factors. After: one bounds the slice rank of a particular three-variable tensor supported on the diagonal, using a decomposition of low-degree polynomials, yielding an exponential improvement.

name: sphere packing in dimension 8
after: Before: the Cohn-Elkies linear programming framework had been in place for over a decade: exhibit a function whose Fourier transform and the function itself satisfy sign conditions, and the resulting bound matches a known lattice packing. What was missing was any such function. After: the required function is constructed explicitly, using modular forms of a particular weight, and satisfies the sign conditions exactly.

name: Vinogradov mean value theorem
after: Before: the number of variables needed for the expected bound grew like k^2 log k, the log factor coming from iterating a descent through many rounds. After: the descent is replaced by a procedure that maintains congruence conditions at every scale simultaneously, removing the accumulation over rounds and reaching the conjectured number of variables.

name: Banaszczyk vector balancing
after: The state is a symmetric convex body; the move replaces it by a convex subset of the union of its two translates; the invariant is that the body's Gaussian measure stays at least one half; the terminal certificate is that a body of measure at least one half contains the origin.

name: Bansal-Jiang Komlos bound
after: The state is a fractional colouring evolving as a diffusion together with a set of alive coordinates; rows are classified by scale and a regularised discrepancy is tracked; a property imposed on the increments of selected row discrepancies yields a decoupling theorem bounding how many rows can be simultaneously near violation, which is what permits the process to move orthogonally to them. Existence of a legal move at each instant is itself a theorem.

name: Guo-Fang-Lu Komlos constant
after: The state is a convex body together with a probability density supported on it; the move is the same body transform as before; the invariant is that the density's total variation in every direction is at most a fixed constant, and this constant survives the move unchanged; the terminal certificate is that a nonempty symmetric convex body contains the origin.
